operations.title: Entry 1401 — Xi Multiplicities Require More Than the Scalar Weyl Model
operations.summary: Atomic mass in a scalar Herglotz model is not eigenspace multiplicity. Residue-sized semisimple amplification repairs the conditional Xi determinant, while the literal principal-ideal quotient has a non-self-adjoint Jordan part at multiple zeros.

operations.title: Residue amplification, not scalar atomic mass, supplies Xi zero multiplicity
operations.statement: Under RH, the scalar minimal Herglotz realization of -Xi'/Xi has one dimension per distinct zero. To obtain the Xi determinant, one must amplify the eigenspace at lambda to dimension m_lambda=-Res_lambda(-Xi'/Xi). The amplified operator is self-adjoint with compact resolvent and the correct determinant, canonically up to unitary equivalence. At a multiple zero the literal principal-ideal entire-function quotient instead has a nilpotent Jordan part and cannot be self-adjoint in a positive metric.
operations.scope: Correction of the conditional determinant model; does not prove RH, simplicity, or source-boundary realization.

operations.title: Ledger 1382 conflated scalar Herglotz mass with eigenspace dimension
operations.statement: The scalar measure m delta_lambda produces a one-dimensional L2 atom, not an m-dimensional eigenspace. Thus the unamplified determinant does not reproduce a multiple zero.

operations.title: Double-zero multiplicity hostile test
operations.description: For F(z)=(z-lambda)^2 compare the one-dimensional atom of mass two, the non-self-adjoint local Jordan quotient, and the semisimple multiplicity-two amplification.

authority_basis.summary: Continue the Xi boundary audit, repair known defects, and add own research to the ledger with claimed sequence numbers.
